title: Why do they hate AI so much?
author: KometUnit1108
selftext:
A little while ago, I posted in a game development community asking what people thought about this idea: doing the front-end work—like creating 3D models—by hand, and letting an AI like Claude handle the programming and placing those 3D models onto the levels. (Looking back now, I think I was pretty dumb to post that in a game developer community.)

Well, I got absolutely slammed for it. Of course, I have the utmost respect for all the creators who put in the time and effort to make amazing games, one by one.

But these days, tools like Claude can actually produce stuff that’s genuinely marketable, and if the ideas are interesting, I think it could work out pretty well. (Of course, I understand there are issues like copyright, but I’d handle those through prompts and do a final review.)

So, ever since I started making games with AI, I’ve been feeling pretty great—I’m finally free from the frustration of having ideas I’m confident in but can’t bring to life.

But why is there still a culture of strong opposition to AI on a global scale?

**Honestly, as long as the idea is solid, the game is well-made, and proper care is taken regarding copyright and other issues, I think it’s perfectly fine.**

**(I’m definitely not making fun of people who create games by hand. On the contrary, since they’re the ones who’ve produced so many wonderful games over the years, I have the utmost respect for them.)**

comments.author: Suecotero
comments.body:
A lot of the people in those spaces made their living and their careers on having this rare and challenging skill: being able to code. 

AI now threatens to automate that because AI is becoming so good at coding that even junior coders are barely needed, and in a few years it's very likely senior coders won't be able to compete on either quality or speed with AI coding. So it looks like it's going to do to them what industrial textiles did to the home weaving industry. And that's terrifying. And scared people are angry.

replies.author: Opulon_Nelva
replies.body:
I know it's scary, but in theory you are individually not the most at risk. I mean, losing jobs is something that happens AI or not.  Be it in the US or in EU, we in average stay at a job 3 years, and half of the time, it's because we are fired from it.

I'm much more worried for entry-levels. All macro data we are getting from the influx of AI-adoption in company is : "we don't take interns and juniors, why would we ?" with the inbound crisis of senior scarcity, and inflation of work-experience.

There is a lot of fear-mongering, not sure you should get cold sweats about needing to go back to plumbing anytime soon. However, you should look with a big curiosity into how the introduction of Excel in the software world destroyed and changed a lot of jobs, forcing a huge amount of people to pivot.

Two days later someone who doesnt even know how to code a "hello world" launches a full game cloned from your demo with AI.

I think it's perfectly understandable why so many game devs hate AI.

I remember myself not being very empathetic for those people, and now it's happening to me.
The tech itself is much more advanced and will affect everyone, but the bottom line is the same, people losing their job.
Same thing happened to farmers or the newspaper industry.
So as I think about my ability to provide for my family, I have to pick a side and be realistic and not hypocritical. I have to adapt for the time I have left on the market.

comments.author: Former-Storm-5087
comments.body:
There are many reasons that others will cover. 
I'll try to cover another one.

You probably already experienced a situation where ChatGPT told you.something so absurdly wrong that righr away you knew it was wrong,  for fun you asked for their reasoning which could be 3.pages long of bullshit and lies ... You read it  probably laughed and carry on. 

But what happens when you no longer have the capacity to detect that bullshit. 

No matter how fast the evolve. AI is always much more advanced at sounding correct than being correct. And as we rely on it we lose the capacity of telling the difference. 

I can give you an example. 
I asked Claude to builde a 3D software that was doing a specific thing I could not get elsewhere. 
It built it as a Webpage. I found it weird but did not pay attention to it. 

I sent it to a friend and he madee realize it did not work for him because somehow it needs an internet connection. (He lost it while testing)

I never asked for it to be relying on cloud.
If it was an actual professional endevor. Sending my content online without knowledge is kind of a big deal. 
The code is in HTML and is completely unreadable to a human. 

How can I know what else is there?

replies.author: KometUnit1108
replies.body:
I see.  
AI can tell lies, after all.
